jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Polite Crime
jokes.joke: I tried joining an outlaw biker gang, but I was raised way too proper. They said, “We ride at midnight.” I said, “Perfect—what’s the dress code?” I lasted one robbery. Apparently when a man points a gun and yells, “Nobody move!” you’re not supposed to lean over and whisper, “He means please.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Charity Gala
jokes.joke: I dated a socialite for two months. Her family had a proper way to do everything. Proper fork for salad, proper fork for fish, proper fork for telling the help you're disappointed in them. I once used the wrong spoon for soup and her mother looked at me like I'd brought a felony into the house. I said, "It's soup, Diane." She said, "It's bisque." I said, "It's still just wet food we're pretending is a lifestyle." We broke up. I kept the spoon out of spite. It's proper now. It's had more therapy than me.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Immersive Dining
jokes.joke: I recently started dating a wealthy socialite, and she loves dragging me to these ultra-exclusive, immersive "farm-to-table" galas. It sounds incredibly elegant, but it’s really just a slaughterhouse with a strict dress code and a jazz quartet. I’m standing in mud in a rented tuxedo, nervously sipping champagne, while a sommelier named Tristan asks if I'd like to look my brisket in the eye.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Polite Stickup
jokes.joke: I always wanted to be an outlaw. But my mom raised me proper. So the one time I tried to rob a liquor store, I waited in line, said please and thank you, and asked if they had change for a hundred. The guy behind the counter gave me a free bottle and a high five. Then he called the cops. Turns out manners don't count as a disguise.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Polished Bandit
jokes.joke: I tried hanging out with a group of outlaws once, just to feel edgy. But I showed up dressed like a socialite at a charity gala. They were comparing scars, and I was like, “I have a blister from new loafers.” One guy asked if I was undercover, and I said, “No, I’m just overdressed.”

scores.comment: Several solid lines and a clear social-class premise, but the therapy tag is generic and weaker than the bisque exchange.
Strong, coherent escalation with vivid imagery; the final brisket line is an effective, non-obvious payoff.
Clean stage rhythm and a respectable final turn, though the overly-polite-criminal premise is familiar and fairly predictable.
Clear and economical, but the overdressed punchline mostly restates the setup rather than delivering a stronger turn.
Clean escalation, strong final line that reinterprets the robbery scene well.
Vivid, unexpected image (sommelier line) with fresh angle on farm-to-table pretension; strongest turn of the set.
Same premise as Joke A but punchline restates the setup rather than snapping; weaker payoff.
Solid setup and imagery, but closing line is flat compared to the blister joke that precedes it.
Very clean stage rhythm and a solid payoff. The polite-criminal premise is a familiar trope, but the whispered 'he means please' lands well.
Starts strong with an excellent rule of three about the forks, but the ending fizzles out by relying on a generic and disconnected therapy trope.
Competent but pedestrian execution of the polite-robber premise. The final punchline feels too expository rather than landing as a joke.
The contrast is clear but overly predictable. It reads more like a quick caption for a single-panel cartoon than a rhythmic stand-up bit.
Clean premise and solid final whisper; familiar proper-vs-criminal shape but well-timed.
Some sharp class lines early, but the spoon-therapy close softens the payoff.
Strong concrete image and non-obvious farm-to-table turn; final line carries cleanly.
Obvious mismatch setup; blister detail mild, final line too soft to land.
Clean premise with a tidy turn; solid but not standout.
Long, with some fun lines, but the payoff softens under the length.
Strong imagery and a clear turn; amusing but not quite excellent.
Straightforward and predictable; mild laugh.
